 Order

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, seek quashing of FIR No.0274/2023 dated 02.05.2023 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S Palam Village, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom, in view of the Settlement dated 20.09.2023 arrived at between the parties before the Mediation Centre,
Dwarka Courts, Delhi whereby the parties have settled all their disputes amicably and are now living together.
2.

This petition is accompanied by the settlement dated 20.09.2023 [Annexure B] and is supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 7714/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:22:52 3.
Petitioner nos.1 to 4 as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned APP for the State has pointed out that as per Memo of Parties, the name of the petitioner no.3 is Raj Bala but in her Aadhar Card, her name has been mentioned as 'Saroj Bala'.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the name of petitioner no.3 is in fact 'Saroj Bala', however, inadvertently it has been mentioned as 'Raj Bala' in the Memo of Parties.
8. Upon hearing the parties, it is directed that the name of petitioner no.3 be read as 'Saroj Bala', as is mentioned in her Aadhar Card.

9. Respondent no.2 affirms the Settlement dated 20.09.2023 and confirms that she has voluntarily settled all her disputes with the petitioners, of her own accord without any duress, coercion or pressure and is now peacefully residing with the petitioners.
She further states that she does not wish to pursue the criminal proceedings against the petitioner and has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

10. In view of the fact that the disputes arise out of matrimonial discord and settlement has been arrived at between the parties, and as the respondent no.2 does not wish to continue with the criminal proceedings, in order to bring a quietus to the present disputes and for the well being of CRL.M.C. 7714/2023 page 2 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:22:52 the children namely Ms. Priyanshi Yadav and Ms. Shriyanshi Yadav, following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs.
State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.
